definition: The share of profits a private equity GP earns above a hurdle rate, typically 20% of fund returns. The mechanism that aligns GP incentives with LP outcomes.
When a PE fund's GP draws down committed capital from LPs to fund an investment. LPs commit upfront but only fund as deals appear during the investment period.
Valuation method that derives intrinsic value as the present value of projected free cash flows plus a terminal value, discounted at the firm's cost of capital.

fullName: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization
definition: EBIT plus non-cash D&A. A rough proxy for operating cash flow before working capital, and the most common base for private-market valuation multiples.
The set of items that reconcile enterprise value to equity value: net debt, minority interest, pension underfunding, preferred stock, and other claims senior to common equity.
Trading multiple computed as enterprise value divided by EBITDA. The default valuation reference in most private equity transactions because it is independent of capital structure.
The private equity firm that manages a fund — sources deals, executes investments, drives operational change, and manages exits. Earns a management fee plus carry on profits above a hurdle.
The discount rate at which the net present value of an investment's cash flows equals zero. The headline annualised return measure for private equity deals; healthy buyout deals target 15–30%.

An acquisition financed largely with debt secured against the target company's own cash flows and assets. Equity contributes a minority of the purchase price and benefits as debt is repaid from operating cash flow.
An investor in a private equity fund. Commits capital that the GP draws down over time, has limited liability, and limited involvement in day-to-day investment decisions.

Total cash returned to investors divided by total cash invested. A simple, time-insensitive measure of how many times the original capital was returned. A 2.0–2.5× MOIC over five years is a typical buyout target.
Total interest-bearing debt minus cash and cash equivalents. Subtracted from enterprise value to bridge to equity value in any standard transaction.
Current operating assets minus current operating liabilities. Changes in NWC are subtracted from operating cash flow because growing businesses tie up cash in receivables and inventory.
The funding ledger of an LBO transaction. Uses (equity purchase price, refinanced debt, fees) must equal Sources (new debt tranches, sponsor equity, rollover equity, cash on balance sheet).
The blended after-tax return debt and equity holders demand for financing the firm. The discount rate in an unlevered DCF.
